items.name: Yogendra Padmasana
items.poseCue: Seated cross-legged; right foot on left thigh, left foot on right thigh with upturned soles; hands resting below navel in Bhairava Mudra.
items.startingPosition: Seated on floor/mat, legs extended straight, no back support; mind relaxed & passively aware.
steps: 1. Place right heel at root of left thigh, sole turned upward.
2. Cross left heel over right thigh, sole upturned.
3. Press knees to ground; heels against pubic bone.
4. Spine straight, chin parallel to floor.
5. Left hand below navel, right hand over left (Bhairava mudra).
6. Close eyes; passively observe breath.
items.breath: Normal rhythmic breathing (passively observe the breath flow).
items.recommendedPractice: Start with 30s–1 min; progress gradually to 10 mins. Alternate crossing of legs.
benefits: Physical: Stretches thighs, calves, knees, ankles.
Therapeutic: Corrects spinal irregularities; relieves sciatica and menstrual issues; boosts abdominal circulation.
Psychological: Focus and mental equanimity.

items.name: Yogendra Sthitaprarthanasana
items.poseCue: Standing tall with feet together, hands folded in front of sternum in classic Namaskar Mudra.
items.startingPosition: Stand erect, feet together/touching, hands at sides; weight balanced heel-to-ball; chin drawn in, slight pelvic tilt.
steps: 1. Fold hands into Namaskar Mudra at center of chest.
2. Keep elbows and shoulders relaxed.
3. Close eyes (or fix gaze straight ahead) and passively observe breath.
items.breath: Normal rhythmic breathing (induces quiet meditative state).
items.recommendedPractice: Initially hold for a few minutes; build up to 10 minutes.
limitations: In vertigo, keep eyes open and feet slightly apart.
benefits: Physical: Body steadiness and neuromuscular coordination.
Therapeutic: Corrects standing posture defects.
Psychological: Calms nervous agitation and promotes poise.

items.name: Yogendra Sukhasana
items.poseCue: Simple cross-legged sitting; each foot placed comfortably under opposite thigh; palms resting on thighs just before knees.
items.startingPosition: Seated flat on mat, legs stretched forward, spine upright.
steps: 1. Bend one leg, placing heel under opposite thigh.
2. Fold other leg similarly under opposite thigh, ankles crossed.
3. Place hands palms down on thighs just before knees.
4. Spine straight, abdomen in normal contour, head poised.
5. Close eyes, observe breath.
items.breath: Normal, gentle rhythmic breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Practice 10 minutes daily. Alternate crossing of legs regularly.
benefits: Physical: Postural correction; stretches calves, thighs, ankles, hips.
Therapeutic: Improves lower extremity flexibility.
Psychological: Grounds thoughts; mindfulness and inner harmony.

items.name: Yogendra Vajrasana
items.poseCue: Kneeling with knees together, sitting in the depression of separated heels; hands resting on knees.
items.startingPosition: Kneeling on mat, knees and toes touching, heels apart.
steps: 1. Lower body to sit in hollow formed between heels and toes.
2. Keep spine, head, and neck in one straight line.
3. Hands placed on respective knees just before patella.
4. Close eyes and observe breath passively.
items.breath: Normal, slow and rhythmic breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Daily practice: 5 minutes, building to 10 minutes. Ideal after meals to boost digestion.
benefits: Physical: Corrects posture automatically; stretches thighs, calves, hips.
Therapeutic: Increases abdominal blood circulation; relieves indigestion, gas, hyperacidity, sciatica, and constipation.
Psychological: Induces mental fixity and calmness.

items.name: Yogendra Parvatasana
items.poseCue: Seated in Padmasana; arms raised straight overhead with palms pressed together, leaning side-to-side, twisting, and folding forward.
items.startingPosition: Seated in Padmasana or Sukhasana, arms at sides, spine erect, gaze forward.
steps: Var 1: Inhale, raise arms overhead, join palms, stretch up. Hold (retention). Exhale, turn palms out, lower arms.
Var 2 (Sideways): Inhale bend right; exhale center; repeat left.
Var 3 (Twist): Exhale twist right; inhale center; repeat left.
Var 4 (Back/Forward): Inhale arch back; exhale bend forward parallel to ground; suspend breath; inhale rise.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1 ratio).
items.recommendedPractice: Var 1: 4 rounds without pause. Var 2–4: 2–3 rounds.
benefits: Physical: Stretches abdominal and pelvic muscles; reduces waist flab.
Therapeutic: Corrects vertebral displacements; massages viscera; relieves uterine prolapse.
Psychological: Develops firm focus, longevity, and stability.

items.name: Yogendra Talasana
items.poseCue: Standing tall on balls of feet with single arm, both parallel arms, or crossed wrists raised vertically overhead.
items.startingPosition: Standing erect, feet parallel 1 foot apart, arms at sides, gaze focused forward.
steps: Talasana 1 (Single Arm): Inhale (3s), raise right arm forward-upward while lifting heels high; hold (6s); exhale (3s), lower arm and heels via backward-downward circuit; repeat left.
Talasana 2: Same, raising both arms parallel palms facing.
Talasana 3: Raise arms sideways, join palms overhead.
Talasana 4: Cross arms at wrists, raise overhead.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). Static hold: normal slow breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 1 round of each variation. Static: 30 secs up to 2 mins.
benefits: Physical: Maximum lengthwise body stretch; tones abdominal wall.
Therapeutic: Expands ribcage & lung capacity; eases joint stiffness; relieves flat feet and sciatica.
Psychological: Promotes poise and emotional balance.

items.name: Yogendra Yastikasana
items.poseCue: Full-body horizontal stretch lying flat on back; arms extended above head on floor, toes pointed downwards.
items.startingPosition: Supine (on back), feet together, heels touching, toes pointing up, arms at sides.
steps: 1. Inhale (3s), swing arms in semi-circular arc overhead until touching floor behind.
2. Simultaneously stretch toes pointing outwards.
3. Hold full-body stretch (6s) with breath retained.
4. Exhale (3s), relax toes, bring arms back to sides.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1); Static hold: normal rhythmic breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 4 rounds per session. Static: Hold 30s to 2 mins.
benefits: Physical: Maximum body stretch (aids height growth in youth); tones abdominal wall.
Therapeutic: Corrects rounded shoulders; improves thoracic breathing; relieves tennis elbow and joint pain.
Psychological: Relieves fatigue and tension.

items.name: Yogendra Hastapadasana
items.poseCue: Standing forward bend; forehead touching knees while hands grasp the ankles.
items.startingPosition: Stand erect, feet together, hands at sides, spine straight, gaze forward.
steps: 1. Inhale (3s), raise arms overhead from front, arch upper torso slightly back.
2. Exhale (3s), bend forward from waist, legs straight.
3. Bend elbows, grasp ankles, pull forehead to rest against knees.
4. Hold with breath suspended (6s).
5. Inhale (3s), release ankles, rise upright with arms overhead, then lower hands to sides.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). Static: normal slow breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 3 rounds with pauses. Static: 30 secs to 2 mins.
benefits: Physical: Extreme stretch to hamstrings, hips, and posterior spine; trims belly fat.
Therapeutic: Massages viscera; relieves constipation and flatulence; stimulates endocrines.
Psychological: Cultivates deep humility, acceptance, and balance.

items.name: Yogendra Paschimottanasana
items.poseCue: Dynamic rowing movement; Static: seated folding forward, hands clasping big toes, forehead resting on knees.
items.startingPosition: Seated, legs straight forward, toes upward, spine erect, hands by sides.
steps: Dynamic (Rowing): Arms folded at chest level; inhale lean back with spine straight; exhale bend forward smoothly, hands passing toes like rowing boat.
Static: Inhale arms up; exhale bend forward, draw abdomen in, clasp big toes, lower elbows, rest forehead between knees. Hold breathing normally.
items.breath: Dynamic: Yogendra smooth rhythm. Static: Normal, slow rhythmic breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 4 continuous cycles = 1 round; do 3–4 rounds. Static: 1 round, holding 30s to 2 mins.
benefits: Physical: Complete stretch of posterior kinetic chain from heels to neck; compresses viscera.
Therapeutic: Relieves constipation, sluggish liver, weak digestion; eases lumbago and sciatica.
Psychological: Reduces stress; calms mental agitation.

items.name: Yogendra Yogamudra
items.poseCue: Seated in Padmasana with hands held behind back (right hand grasping left wrist), bending forward and sideways to knees.
items.startingPosition: Seated in Padmasana or Sukhasana, hands clasped behind back (right hand holding left wrist).
steps: 1. Exhale (3s), bend forward arching spine until forehead/crown touches mat.
2. Hold with breath suspended (6s).
3. Inhale (3s), gently raise head and straighten spine.
4. Exhale (3s), twist upper torso right and touch forehead to right knee; hold (6s); inhale return.
5. Repeat to left knee to complete 1 round.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). Static: normal slow breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 3 rounds with pauses. Static: Hold forward bend 30s to 2 mins.
limitations: Severe back problems, slip disc, cervical/lumbar spondylosis
benefits: Physical: Stretches posterior trunk muscles; tones viscera.
Therapeutic: Compresses colon, curing constipation; relieves gas, lumbar pain; counters uterine laxity.
Psychological: Cultivates surrender, modesty, and serenity.

items.name: Yogendra Bhujangasana
items.poseCue: Prone; palms under shoulders, peeling upper spine off the ground vertebra by vertebra like a cobra raising its hood. Navel remains on mat.
items.startingPosition: Prone (on stomach), legs straight, feet together, toes out; palms flat beside chest, elbows close, forehead on mat.
steps: 1. Lift head and neck; inhaling (3s), use back muscles to lift shoulders, thorax, and upper abdomen vertebra by vertebra.
2. Arch spine back, feeling progressive contraction from cervical down to sacrum.
3. Hold posture with breath retained (6s).
4. Exhaling (3s), carefully lower spine in reverse order (lumbar, thoracic, cervical) until forehead touches mat.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). Static hold: normal slow rhythmic breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 3 rounds with pauses. Static: 30 secs up to 2 mins.
benefits: Physical: Deep tone to spinal extensors; massages adrenal glands; posterior abdominal stretch.
Therapeutic: Deepens breathing; resolves minor vertebral misalignments; eases kyphosis and menstrual pain.
Psychological: Develops willpower, boldness, and alertness.

items.name: Yogendra Dhanurvakrasana
items.poseCue: Prone; knees bent and hands grasping ankles; pulling upward so torso and thighs form the taut curve of an archer's bow.
items.startingPosition: Prone (on belly), forehead on mat, legs straight, toes pointed; bend knees, grasp respective ankles firmly.
steps: 1. Inhaling (3s), raise head and chest upwards, arching spine.
2. Simultaneously pull ankles upward and backward to lift thighs off the mat.
3. Balance entire body weight centrally on navel region.
4. Hold pose with breath retained (6s).
5. Exhaling (3s), lower chest and thighs, release ankles.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). Static: normal slow breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 3 rounds with rest between. Static: 30 secs to 2 mins.
benefits: Physical: Arches full spine; opens chest and shoulders; strengthens thighs and arms.
Therapeutic: Strong intra-abdominal massage; relieves stubborn constipation and flatulence; helps manage diabetes.
Psychological: Dispels lethargy; boosts stamina and determination.

items.name: Yogendra Shalabhasana
items.poseCue: Prone; chin resting on floor, palms under thighs, elevating straight legs backward-upward like a locust.
items.startingPosition: Prone (on stomach), chin on mat, legs stretched straight, toes pointed; arms alongside thighs, palms facing down.
steps: 1. Exhaling (3s), contract lower back to raise right leg high without tilting hips.
2. Hold with breath suspended (6s).
3. Inhaling (3s), lower right leg smoothly.
4. Repeat with left leg.
5. Now exhale (3s) and raise both straight legs simultaneously; hold (6s); inhale (3s) lower to floor (1 round).
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1).
items.recommendedPractice: 3 rounds with pauses between.
benefits: Physical: Strengthens wrists, lower back, gluteals, hamstrings, and diaphragm.
Therapeutic: Relieves mild sciatica, backache, cervical spondylitis; tones liver and intestines.
Psychological: Builds self-confidence and fortitude.

items.name: Yogendra Konasana – I & II
items.poseCue: Standing with wide stance; lateral side bending of spine without twisting or moving below waist.
items.startingPosition: Stand erect, feet 2 to 2.5 feet apart and parallel; spine upright, gaze forward.
steps: Konasana 1: Left hand on waist; inhale, look down at right hand and bend torso right, sliding right hand to knee and left hand up to armpit; hold (retention); exhale return; repeat left.
Konasana 2: Raise left arm straight close to ear; inhale bend torso right, curving spine laterally; hold (retention); exhale return; repeat left.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). Inhale (3s) – Hold (6s) – Exhale (3s).
items.recommendedPractice: 2 rounds of each technique with pauses.
benefits: Physical: Tones lateral waist obliques; trims waistline.
Therapeutic: Compresses abdominal viscera alternately; relieves shoulder/lumbar stiffness; aids digestion.
Psychological: Synchronizes mind-body awareness; alleviates nervous depression.

items.name: Yogendra Trikonasana – II
items.poseCue: Feet wide apart (3+ ft); right foot turned 90°; bending laterally to touch right toe, left arm reaching straight up to ceiling, gaze fixed on raised left thumb.
items.startingPosition: Stand straight, feet 3 to 3.5 feet apart; arms raised sideways at shoulder level, palms forward.
steps: 1. Inhale, turn right foot 90° out and gaze at right thumb.
2. Exhale (3s), bend laterally right, touch right toe with right fingers; raise left arm vertically to ceiling; turn neck to gaze at left thumb.
3. Hold with breath suspended (6s).
4. Inhale (3s), look down at right thumb and rise upright.
5. Repeat on left side to complete 1 round.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). Static: normal slow breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 3 rounds. Static: Hold 1 minute each side alternately.
benefits: Physical: Stretches lateral trunk; trims waistline.
Therapeutic: Alternating visceral compression aids digestion; promotes blood circulation.
Psychological: Stimulates nervous system; alleviates depression.

items.name: Yogendra Konasana – III
items.poseCue: Standing wide stance; twisting torso forward diagonally so right hand touches left toe while left arm points straight up.
items.startingPosition: Stand straight, feet 2.5 feet apart; arms extended in front at shoulder height, palms up.
steps: 1. Inhale, spread arms out to sides in line with shoulders; gaze at right palm.
2. Exhale (3s), swing arms, bend forward and twist spine so right fingers touch left toes, left arm pointing straight up to ceiling; look up at left palm.
3. Hold with breath suspended (6s).
4. Inhale (3s), rise, untwist back to center.
5. Repeat swinging to opposite side.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1).
items.recommendedPractice: 3 rounds with pauses.
limitations: Slipped disc, facet joint problems, scoliosis
benefits: Physical: Stretches waist, hamstrings, and shoulders; improves spinal rotation.
Therapeutic: Corrects scoliosis and ankylosing spondylitis; gives visceral organ massage.
Psychological: Brings inward poise and body-mind harmony.

items.name: Yogendra Vakrasana – I
items.poseCue: Seated; legs straight; arms at shoulder level swinging and twisting torso horizontally to the side.
items.startingPosition: Seated, legs straight forward, feet together, spine straight, arms raised forward to shoulder level, palms down.
steps: 1. Exhale, smoothly swing arms and twist spine to the right as far as possible.
2. Inhale, immediately return to center.
3. Exhale, twist smoothly to the left.
4. Inhale, return to center (completing 1 round).
items.breath: Synchronized breathing with movement (dynamic smooth swing).
items.recommendedPractice: 3 rounds with pauses.
limitations: Acute or resolving disc prolapse (slipped disc)
benefits: Physical: Loosens spinal vertebrae; tones waist muscles.
Therapeutic: Alleviates stiffness; stimulates digestive peristalsis.
Psychological: Increases alertness and coordination.

items.name: Yogendra Vakrasana – II
items.poseCue: Standing with feet shoulder-width apart; swinging arms and trunk dynamically into a full horizontal torso twist.
items.startingPosition: Stand erect, feet 2 to 2.5 feet apart, arms extended forward at shoulder height, palms down.
steps: 1. Exhale, swing arms to right, twisting spine; bend left elbow while extending right arm straight back, gazing at right thumb.
2. Inhale, return to center.
3. Exhale, repeat twist to left side, gazing at left thumb.
4. Inhale, return to center (1 round).
items.breath: Synchronized rhythmic breathing (dynamic continuous movement).
items.recommendedPractice: 3 rounds with pauses.
benefits: Physical: Strengthens lower back muscles; tones lateral abdominal wall.
Therapeutic: Alleviates lumbar stiffness; reduces flank fat.
Psychological: Sharpens mental concentration and agility.

items.name: Yogendra Vakrasana – III
items.englishName: Supine Twist – Both Knees Bent Together
items.poseCue: Supine; arms spread wide, knees bent and stacked together; dropping knees to the right floor while head turns left.
items.startingPosition: Supine (on back), arms outstretched perpendicular to torso (T-shape); knees bent, feet & knees together flat on floor.
steps: 1. Exhale (3s), drop both knees together to the right until right knee touches mat.
2. Simultaneously turn head left to gaze at left thumb.
3. Hold with breath suspended (6s).
4. Inhale (3s), bring knees and head back to center.
5. Exhale (3s), drop knees left, turn head right; hold (6s); inhale return.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1).
items.recommendedPractice: 3 rounds with pauses.
benefits: Physical: Relaxes spinal musculature; stretches hips.
Therapeutic: Excellent for low back pain and sacroiliac relief; mobilizes vertebrae.
Psychological: Calming and deeply grounding.

items.name: Yogendra Vakrasana – IV
items.poseCue: Supine; knees bent but feet kept apart; dropping legs so left knee rests on floor near right ankle.
items.startingPosition: Supine, arms outstretched perpendicular to body; knees bent with feet and knees kept hip-width apart.
steps: 1. Exhale (3s), drop knees together to right so left knee rests near right ankle.
2. Simultaneously turn neck left to gaze at left thumb.
3. Hold with breath suspended (6s).
4. Inhale (3s), return to center; repeat to opposite side.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1).
items.recommendedPractice: 3 rounds with pauses.
benefits: Physical: Deep stretch to piriformis, outer hip, and lumbar region.
Therapeutic: Alleviates sciatic nerve compression and pelvic stiffness.
Psychological: Relieves fatigue; calms central nervous system.

items.name: Yogendra Ekpadasana
items.poseCue: Standing balance on right leg; left foot pressed against right inner groin, palms joined in Namaskar at chest.
items.startingPosition: Stand erect, feet together, arms at sides, gaze focused at one point straight ahead.
steps: 1. Lift left leg with hands, placing left heel tightly against right groin, sole flat against inner thigh, toes pointing down.
2. Once balance is secured, join palms in Namaskar Mudra at chest center.
3. Hold posture gazing fixedly at a point, breathing normally.
4. Slowly release leg and repeat balance on opposite leg.
items.breath: Normal continuous breathing (focus on steady, slow breath).
items.recommendedPractice: Practice morning and evening; hold from a few seconds building to 2–3 mins per leg.
limitations: Sciatica, slipped disc, acute lower back pain
benefits: Physical: Strengthens legs and spine; improves balance and corrects flat feet.
Therapeutic: Isometric hold strengthens bones (benefits osteoporosis); improves extremity circulation in diabetes.
Psychological: Sharpens concentration, equanimity, and presence.

items.name: Yogendra Utkatasana
items.poseCue: Squatting low on tiptoes with arms extended parallel to the floor in front. Derived from wrestler's Danda Baithak.
items.startingPosition: Stand erect, feet parallel 1 foot apart, arms at sides, gaze fixed forward.
steps: 1. Inhale (3s), stretch arms forward parallel to ground, simultaneously raise heels balancing on balls of feet.
2. Exhale (3s), lower body into full squat, thighs pressed against calves, balancing on tiptoes with arms forward.
3. Hold squat with breath suspended (6s).
4. Inhale (3s), rise up smoothly on tiptoes; retain breath (6s); exhale lower arms and heels.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). (Avoid breath holding if cardiac condition is present).
items.recommendedPractice: 4 rounds with pauses.
limitations: Moderate to severe osteoarthritis of knees
benefits: Physical: Strengthens quadriceps, calves, ankles, and pelvic floor; engages core.
Therapeutic: Aids weight loss around hips; relieves joint and back dull aches.
Psychological: Cultivates fierce determination and physical stability.

items.name: Yogendra Bhadrasana
items.poseCue: Seated with knees bent outward, soles of feet pressed together close to perineum, hands pressing knees gently towards floor.
items.startingPosition: Seated, legs straight forward, feet together, hands by sides, spine tall.
steps: 1. Inhale, bend knees outward, draw feet in with soles pressed together.
2. Bring heels close to perineum/generative organ (clasp feet if needed).
3. Place hands on respective knees, gently pressing them toward floor.
4. Maintain posture with an erect spine and normal breathing.
5. Straighten legs to release. (Optional: gentle butterfly flapping of knees as a warm-up).
items.breath: Normal, slow and rhythmic breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Practice daily for 1–2 minutes comfortably.
limitations: Acute pain in knee or hip joints
benefits: Physical: Deep stretch to inner thighs, groins, and hips; releases pelvic stiffness.
Therapeutic: Aids blood flow to pelvis; relieves lower backache and piles; aids labor when practiced during pregnancy.
Psychological: Clears fatigue; calms and centers the mind.

items.name: Yogendra Matsyasana
items.poseCue: Supine; legs folded in Padmasana or Sukhasana; elbows bent under head, hands clasping opposite elbows resting on floor above head.
items.startingPosition: Supine (on back), feet together, hands by sides, body relaxed.
steps: 1. Fold legs into Sukhasana or Padmasana while lying supine.
2. Draw arms from sides behind head, bending elbows.
3. Clasp opposite elbows with hands and let forearms rest on floor above crown.
4. Maintain position breathing rhythmically.
5. Unclasp elbows, return arms to sides, unfold legs.
items.breath: Normal rhythmic breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Practice for 1–2 minutes per session.
benefits: Physical: Massages thoracic and abdominal organs; strengthens pelvic floor.
Therapeutic: Stretches neck to regulate thyroid & thymus; relieves bleeding piles, constipation, uterine prolapse, and incontinence.
Psychological: Induces peace; dispels stress and irritability.

items.name: Yogendra Pavanmuktasana
items.poseCue: Supine; knees pulled tightly against chest, arms wrapped around shins clasping opposite elbows.
items.startingPosition: Supine (on back), feet together, arms by sides, mind calm.
steps: Var 1 (Single Leg): Inhale, then exhale (3s) bending right knee to chest, interlacing fingers over shin to press knee firmly to chest; hold suspended (6s); inhale (3s) release; repeat left.
Var 2 (Both Legs): Exhale (3s), bend both knees to chest, wrap forearms around shins clasping opposite elbows; hold suspended (6s); inhale (3s) release.
items.breath: Yes: Yogendra Rhythm (3:6:3 or 1:2:1). Static: normal slow breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Dynamic: 4 rounds with pauses. Static: 30 secs to 2 mins.
benefits: Physical: Massages visceral organs; stretches lower back and hips.
Therapeutic: Directly releases gas and relieves flatulence; cures chronic constipation and sluggish liver; remedies flabby abdomen.
Psychological: Clears mental sluggishness via toxin elimination.

items.name: Yogendra Ardha-Sarvangasana
items.poseCue: Inverted; trunk angled at ~45° supported by palms on hips, elbows on mat, legs held straight; chin tucked in jugular notch.
items.startingPosition: Supine on mat, feet together, arms by sides, body relaxed, full breath taken.
steps: 1. Exhaling, bend knees to thighs and using abdominal muscles, raise lower body vertically.
2. Place hands under hips (fingers supporting hips, thumbs above) to support weight.
3. Balance weight upon palms, elbows, and shoulders. Chin set in jugular notch.
4. Hold pose breathing normally (max 2 mins).
5. Inhaling, lower hips gently down using hands as brakes.
items.breath: Normal, slow and rhythmic breathing (Never retain breath in inversions).
items.recommendedPractice: Practice once per session, from 20 seconds up to 2 minutes. Can use wall/pillows initially.
benefits: Physical: Strengthens shoulders and arms; nourishes brain with venous blood flow.
Therapeutic: Stimulates thyroid, parathyroid, and pituitary glands; drains venous stasis from lower limbs (prevents varicose veins and hemorrhoids); tones sagging abdomen.
Psychological: Calms nervous system; relieves mood swings.

items.name: Yogendra Sarvangasana
items.poseCue: Full vertical candle pose; chest pressed into chin, trunk perpendicular to mat, palms supporting upper-mid back.
items.startingPosition: Supine on mat, legs together, hands beside body, breath settled.
steps: 1. Exhaling, raise straight legs to 90°.
2. Raise arms to hold waist, pushing body up into vertical alignment with elbows resting on floor.
3. Shift hands lower down back toward scapulae, extending fingers along ribs.
4. Chin firmly locked into jugular notch (chin lock), full body weight on shoulders.
5. Hold breathing normally (up to 2 mins).
6. Inhaling, bend knees slightly and roll down slowly vertebra by vertebra.
items.breath: Normal, slow and rhythmic breathing (No breath retention).
items.recommendedPractice: Practice once, 20 seconds up to 2 minutes.
benefits: Physical: Total-body venous drainage; strengthens shoulder girdle.
Therapeutic: Powerful regulator of endocrine glands (thyroid/pituitary); relieves dyspepsia, hemorrhoids, and headache; boosts immunity.
Psychological: Relieves mental stress; increases confidence and self-reliance.

items.name: Yogendra Shavasana
items.poseCue: Supine, legs 1.5–2 ft apart relaxed outward, arms 1 ft from sides, palms up, body motionless like a corpse.
items.startingPosition: Lie supine, face towards sky, shoulders rested, arms 1 foot from body, legs 1.5–2 feet apart, facial muscles loose.
steps: Partial Shavasana: Close eyes; sequentially relax the 16 vital points (Marmasthanani: toes, ankles, knees, thighs/arms, anus, genitals, navel, abdomen, chest, neck, lips, nose tip, eyes, eyebrow center, forehead, crown).
Full Shavasana: Consciously shut down all nervous stimuli simultaneously; forget body consciousness; allow slow diaphragmatic breathing.
items.breath: Continuous, deep and rhythmic diaphragmatic breathing.
items.recommendedPractice: Practice for at least 5 minutes daily. Roll onto right side before sitting up.
benefits: Physical: Relieves voluntary muscular and nervous tension; normalizes pulse and respiration.
Therapeutic: Alleviates insomnia, headaches, and high blood pressure; restorative to organs.
Psychological: Induces profound mental tranquility, meditation, and resets stress responses.
